name: EV battery recycling and circular materials
summary: Industrial companies use metallurgy skills to recover materials and make battery components from used EV batteries, usually through joint ventures. Two consultancy case summaries describe early-stage efforts. Neither gives revenue or profit figures.
how_it_makes_money: Not disclosed in the sources. Assumption: sale of recovered materials or battery components, possibly plus fees for taking back batteries. One case page mentions an as-a-service offer that bundles maintenance and recycling, with no prices.

hardware: Pilot recycling plant (under construction at the nuclear-technology group, per the source)
Production facilities for battery components (joint ventures in northern France)
partners: Ecosystem partners along the supply chain
regulation: Regulatory hurdles are named as a source of uncertainty
financing: Investment decisions staged over time against market readiness
data: Assumptions about battery return volumes drove the financial projections

stakeholder_value.provider: New business line using existing metallurgy skills
stakeholder_value.partner: Roles in a shared ecosystem or joint venture

what_must_be_true: Enough used-battery input volume (the source calls volumes uncertain)
Partner roles in the ecosystem are agreed; existing partnerships can block entry in some regions
Regulation settles in a workable way
Investment is staged against market development

risks_failure_causes.text: Return volumes of used batteries are uncertain
Longer timelines than typical product launches
Existing partnerships blocked entry in some regions, so the group narrowed its focus to domestic opportunities
Technical feasibility was confirmed but target customers, regions and value-chain position were still unclear

cases.note: Joint ventures for battery components in northern France were started and a pilot recycling plant is under development. No commercial results reported.

The consultancy says the supplier tripled its recycling rate and raised recycling effectiveness to 98 percent, with a joint venture with a smaller recycling partner. No baseline or financials given. The site describes this as battery recycling, but the case page reads like a refractory-materials service, so the EV battery link is unclear.
